extracted.intended_audience: Wikipedia readers and editors (especially those editing biographies of living persons)
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article (encyclopedic entry) about a living person — here, the poet Patricia Smith — with embedded editorial templates and metadata that state sourcing, style, and completeness expectations for the article. The page is meant for general readers but also carries guidance for contributors on verification and removal of contentious material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biography of a living person: needs additional citations for verification
rubrics_metrics.description: "This biography of a living person needs additional citations for verification. Please help by adding reliable sources."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim template text instructing editors to add reliable sources to verify claims in the article. It flags the article as lacking sufficient citations and requests improvement by adding verifiable references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal requirement for contentious material about living persons
rubrics_metrics.description: "Contentious material about living persons that is unsourced or poorly sourced must be removed immediately from the article and its talk page, especially if potentially libelous."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong policy directive: any potentially libelous or contentious statements about a living person that lack reliable sourcing should be promptly removed rather than merely tagged; applies both to article content and related talk-page discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended types of sources to find
rubrics_metrics.description: "Find sources: 'Patricia Smith' poet – news · newspapers · books · scholar · JSTOR (July 2022) (Learn how and when to remove this message)"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The template lists example source types deemed appropriate for verification (news, newspapers, books, academic databases such as JSTOR, Google Scholar). Editors are guided toward these source classes when adding citations to satisfy the BLP notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article completeness: 'This list is incomplete; you can help' notice
rubrics_metrics.description: "This list is incomplete; you can help by adding missing items."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A maintenance note indicating that the bibliography/works list (and possibly other lists) is incomplete and inviting contributors to expand the coverage by adding missing works or items, with an associated timestamp (e.g., April 2015).

rubrics_metrics.name: Date-format/style note: use mdy dates
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stylistic/formatting instruction (metadata) indicating the preferred date format for the article (month-day-year). This reflects site-wide/local formatting conventions to ensure consistency.
